contract: clock_ticks returns libc sysconf(_SC_CLK_TCK) cast to f64, including -1 on failure. It supplies the divisor for process CPU time; the times call and arithmetic remain outside this increment.
fixtures: Compare against the native getconf CLK_TCK utility, then separately probe successful-query errno preservation using zero, EIO and an arbitrary raw sentinel. Restore the caller errno before assertions. These are native system-boundary checks, not mocked command-I/O tests.
candidate: Existing nix 0.31.3 unistd::sysconf exposes CLK_TCK and returns Result<Option<c_long>>. Inspected source clears errno before calling libc exactly once; unlike the direct call, that can erase a caller errno. Safe Errno::last_raw and set_raw can restore the incoming value when the call leaves zero errno. Mapping None and Err to -1 preserves the numeric sentinel; retain any nonzero errno produced by the native call.
limits: Native fixtures establish supported-platform behavior, not every injected libc implementation. Investigate whether restoration preserves the actual platform contract before replacement. Do not broaden this into processor-count changes or claim a system-only exception.
deletion: If compatibility is demonstrated, delete the direct sysconf unsafe block in this task; do not keep a parallel implementation. No API or version change is planned.
